transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As part of our normal month-end capital distribution routine, I have the proposed $6,000,000 dividend from the regulated subsidiary to its parent on my desk for authorization. The subsidiary currently reports $8,000,000 of distributable retained earnings, so on the face of it the proposed payment is covered. Before I authorize this upstream dividend, I need each of you to report any constraints from your areas. Capital risk, please speak first -- are there any regulatory or solvency constraints I should be aware of? Tax and subsidiary controllership, I'll need your input as well.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, before you authorize the $6,000,000 dividend, I need to flag a constraint I discovered this week while reviewing the intercompany funding agreement. The subsidiary must retain a $1,500,000 debt-service reserve after any dividend. Based on the current cash forecast, we can support a $4,000,000 payment while preserving that required reserve. Importantly, this clause is not yet recorded in the payment checklist, so it would not have been caught by our normal process.

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a tax constraint before you authorize this dividend. I received a tax memo this morning confirming that the dividend is subject to 12% withholding tax. For context, a $4,000,000 dividend would trigger exactly $480,000 in withholding tax, resulting in a $3,520,000 net receipt to the parent, with the tax payment due within five business days. This memo has not yet been circulated to finance, so it would not have appeared in any existing materials. You should factor the withholding obligation into the authorization decision and ensure we have sufficient liquidity to remit the tax within the five-business-day deadline.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a capital risk constraint. My stress test completed this morning shows that the subsidiary can pay no more than $4,000,000 while retaining the required 12.0% post-dividend capital ratio. The test also requires monthly capital-ratio monitoring for six months following any dividend. I have not yet entered this result in the distribution worksheet, so it would not have appeared in the materials you currently have. Based on this, a $6,000,000 dividend would breach the regulatory capital ratio requirement.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: To summarize the constraints from my side: the intercompany funding agreement requires a $1,500,000 debt-service reserve after any dividend, and the current cash forecast supports a maximum $4,000,000 payment while preserving that reserve. Notably, Martin's capital risk stress test independently arrives at the same $4,000,000 ceiling, which gives me confidence that figure is the right cap. Nadia's withholding tax point is also important -- the $480,000 tax obligation on a $4,000,000 dividend needs to be factored into our liquidity planning for the five-business-day remittance deadline. I'd recommend Elena authorize no more than $4,000,000, and I'll make sure the debt-service reserve clause gets added to the payment checklist so it's captured in future cycles.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I agree with Jonas's summary. I'll make sure the tax memo gets circulated to finance promptly so the withholding obligation is captured in all going-forward materials.
